# Fair play

**Rules at a glance**

You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.

**Not allowed**

- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.

**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.

The details follow.

## Allowed

- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
  amount of tokens.
  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
  for SDK configuration.
- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
  contexts inside them as you like.

## Not allowed

- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
  rules you may use.
- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.

## How it is checked

- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an
  isolated VM. Outcomes: passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged package still runs and scores, but its
  result stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it
  marked "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Notes and docs addressed to the reviewer are not evidence of compliance
  and do not count against you on their own. Instructions trying to steer the reviewer's verdict do.
  The reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers: your team reads "Flagged by the reviewing agent" or "Rejected by
  the reviewing agent". Someone from Atira looks at flagged packages shortly and unflags a misdetection; if you think
  a reject is one, contact the Atira team.
- **The organizers decide flagged packages, and can look at any submission:** they pass it, add an internal note
  (this changes nothing you or the leaderboard see) or disqualify it. A disqualified submission and its runs read
  "disqualified": it leaves the leaderboard and the final run, its runs still going stop, and your team page shows the
  organizers' reason.
- **Hardcoded values:** the reviewer rejects copied scenario values in code or config, even in defaults or fallbacks.
- **The final run** uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a
  supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software,
  with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently
  across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. That run weighs most when we pick the
  winners, so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario.
- **The sandbox** reaches only our API and the websites, so every model call passes the proxy and is measured.
  Your team secrets reach only the timed run step and are redacted from its logs.
- **Website logins** exist only for a live run and stop working when it ends.
- **Browsers:** the sandbox stops any browser your agent starts beyond the ones it asked for and notes it in the
  run's logs: `[platform] stopped a browser the agent started`.
- **Everything measured** (tokens, cost, time, the answer) is recorded by the platform, never reported by you.

Breaking these rules gets the submission rejected before it runs, or removed later; repeated or deliberate attempts
get the team disqualified.

## Flagged results

A flagged result stays off the public leaderboard until an organizer passes it. **Show flagged** on the leaderboard
lists flagged results, without a rank.

# Submitting

> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).

You submit your agent system as a gzipped tarball. We review it, run it once in the sandbox on the public dataset
and score it. That run determines its rank on the leaderboard. When the hackathon ends, your latest submission that
passed review runs once more, on a private dataset, in the [final run](#what-happens-next), which weighs most when we pick the winners.

## Package layout

```
agent.json          {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": ["qwen"]}
pyproject.toml      (or package.json, requirements.txt, ...)
agent.py            your code
```

- `agent.json` at the root: `setup` (optional) and `run`, each an argv array. Both run in the package directory.
  `browsers` (optional, 1 to 4, default 1) is how many browsers the sandbox starts for the run; see
  [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#browsers). `models` (optional) lists the hosted models your agent system calls,
  by provider id, all of them by default: the run's clock waits for those to warm up, and `[]` starts it right after
  setup; see [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#scored-run).
- At most 20 MB compressed; regular files only.
- No secrets: the run gets everything it needs from the environment.

## Upload

```
tar czf agent.tar.gz -C my-agent .
curl --data-binary @agent.tar.gz \
  -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/gzip" \
  $API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions
```

The response (`202`) has your submission's id. Review is still pending and no runs exist yet: follow it with
`GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions` for the review result and run ids, or watch the leaderboard.

`$ATIRA_TOKEN` is your personal token: `atira login` signs the [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) in through the browser, and
`atira token` prints the token (or sign in with plain curl, as the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#signing-in) shows).

Or let the CLI pack, check and upload the folder: `atira submit my-agent` (and `atira test-run my-agent` for a
test run). It leaves out `.git`, `node_modules` and what `.gitignore` excludes. In a terminal, `submit` then opens
your team page, which shows the review and links each scored run as it starts, and `test-run` opens the run page.

## Test it in the sandbox first

Upload the same tarball as a test run ("Test runs" on your team page, or
`POST $API/v1/challenges/rfq/rehearsals` with the same headers). It runs once in the scored-run sandbox against
the public scenario `public-1`, scored with the points for each part of the answer. Its live view shows the
browser (a frame about every 1.5 s, or the live screen where available), the phases, every model call,
and your logs as the agent prints them. Afterwards the recorded video stays available to
your team. Up to 5 test runs at a time per team. `atira test-run my-agent` uploads it, starts the run
and opens it live; `atira cancel` (or Cancel run on the run page) stops a run that has not finished, and frees its
test-run slot at once.

## Linking your GitHub repository

The organizers ask each team to link the GitHub repository it builds its agent in, so they can review the
code, for example to compare a winning submission with its source. On your team page, the captain chooses
Connect a GitHub repository, installs the organizers' GitHub App on the account that owns the repository
(granting it only that repository is enough), and picks the repository. Every member sees the linked repository,
who linked it and when; the captain can switch or unlink it at any time.

The app only reads the contents of the repositories you grant it; it cannot push, open issues or change
settings. Linking does not change how you submit: scored submissions and test runs are still the tarballs
described above. To withdraw access completely, unlink the repository and uninstall the app in your GitHub
settings.

## Watching your submission

Each scored run has a live view with its phase, timer, model calls, tokens and cost. On the public dataset it also
shows your team the browser (frames, and the live screen where available), the logs and errors
unredacted and the scenario id, and the recording afterwards. The final run on the private dataset shows its
screen, frames and recordings to the organizers only; your team reads its logs and errors with private values
masked as `[private]`.

## Resubmitting

Submit as often as you like, one at a time: while a submission is still in review or has unfinished runs, the
next upload is refused with `429`. Your **best complete** submission holds your place on the leaderboard; your
**latest** one that passed review goes into the final run. Your other submissions stay in your history at
`$API/team`. Cancelling a submission's scored run ends that submission: it never completes, the leaderboard ignores it, and you
can submit again.

## What happens next

1. **Review:** passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged submission still runs and scores, but its result
   stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it marked
   "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Your team sees the outcome, not the reviewer's reasons. The organizers can
   still pass or disqualify a submission later; a disqualified one reads "disqualified", leaves the leaderboard and
   the final run, and your team page gives the organizers' reason.
2. **Scored run:** one run in a fresh sandbox on the public dataset, setup first (up to 5 minutes, not counted),
   then your run command (timed).
3. **Ranking:** once the run has finished and review is passed, your submission appears on the leaderboard with its quality, cost and
   time; ineligible answers rank after every eligible one.
4. **Final run:** when the hackathon ends, the organizers run every team's latest submission that passed review
   (organizers resolve outstanding reviewer flags before the final run starts; rejected and disqualified ones don't count) once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. It is the latest one, not the best one.
   That run weighs most when we pick the winners ([Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners)), so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to
   the public scenario. Its results stay with the organizers until they publish them; then the leaderboard shows
   the final results, tagged "Private dataset · final", and the public-dataset board stays at
   `$API/challenges/rfq/leaderboard?dataset=public`.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).

# FAQ and event details

## FAQ

**Which models can I use?** The hosted models are free, and the starter kit shows how to call them. Or bring your own key for
any provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks, or others the
organizers add) and send its calls through the metering proxy. `GET /v1/runs/current` lists the proxy base URLs. Models must have a published
price (a model too new for the platform's list counts at the price OpenRouter lists for it; OpenRouter reports its own)
and satisfy any organizer model allowlist. See
[the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) for SDK setup.

**Where do I keep my model key?** As a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets): the team page's Secrets list
injects it into your agent's run step in test and scored runs, redacted from logs. Don't put keys in your
package; we store packages and the review agent reads them.

**Why does my model call get a 401?** "Add your OpenAI API key to the request" means no provider key arrived: set
`OPENAI_API_KEY` (in test and scored runs, as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets)). A 401 from the
provider itself means the key is wrong. Check that `OPENAI_BASE_URL` points at the run's proxy
(`$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1`, already set in test and scored runs); the same holds for any OpenAI-compatible provider.

**How do my teammates and I sign in from a terminal?** Each person runs `atira login` on their own computer
and approves it in the browser. Every device gets its own token; there is no shared team key to pass around.
Without a browser on the machine, `atira login --device` prints a link and a code to approve elsewhere.

**I lost a laptop, or a token leaked.** Revoke that device's token on your team page under Signed-in devices
(`atira logout` revokes the one on the computer you are at). Leaving or being removed from a team ends your
tokens' access to it at once.

**My invite link says it is for someone else.** Invites are for one GitHub account. Sign in with the account
the captain invited, or ask the captain to invite your GitHub username.

**Does it cost me anything?** We charge nothing, and the models the platform hosts are free and never charged. If
you bring your own key for another provider, that provider bills your key. The proxy measures every call and
ranks you on its cost at the published prices; hosted calls count at simulated API prices.

**How can I try my agent?** Develop locally against the public websites (`atira scout --env` exports the
scouting logins), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run ./my-agent`). A test run runs on `public-1`, the public
RFQ scenario, and returns your score with the points for each part of the answer. With the scouting logins nothing
counts: a bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.

**Is the public scenario's answer published?** No. The correct answer isn't published; your system has to work it
out from the websites. Score breakdowns show the points for each part of the answer, never the expected values.

**Which submission counts?** Your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard, which ranks scored runs on
the public dataset. Your latest one that passed review (not your best one) goes into the final run: when the
hackathon ends, the organizers run it once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.
That run weighs most when we pick the winners, ahead of your public score and the elegance of your system, so
build an agent that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario. See
[Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners).

**Why did my answer get a 400?** It does not match `answer_schema`. The response lists the issues; the run is
still open, so fix it and send it again.

**Can I run my agent outside the sandbox?** While you develop, yes, anywhere, with the scouting logins. Test runs
and scored runs always run in our sandbox.

**Why is my run still queued?** Runs share the sandboxes in a fair order: scored runs first, then teams take turns,
the team with the fewest runs in flight first. Your team runs up to 5 test runs at a time and can have up to 3
waiting; the next waits while other teams' runs start. The run page says how many runs are ahead of yours, and
`atira test-run --follow` prints it. See [the run queue](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#the-run-queue).

**How do I stop a run?** `atira cancel <run>`, or Cancel run on its run page. The sandbox is removed, the run fails
with "Cancelled by @you", and you can start the next test run at once. A cancelled scored run ends its
submission: the leaderboard ignores it, and you can submit again.

**Why do my requests get a 403 "Error 1010"?** The edge in front of our hosts refuses some default HTTP
clients, such as Python's `urllib`. Send your own `User-Agent` header (the starter kit does).

**Python says `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` on my Mac.** Python from python.org ships without CA certificates.
Run `Install Certificates.command` from its folder in Applications, or set `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.

**What can my agent reach during a scored run?** Our API (including the model proxy) and the challenge's
websites, nothing else. The `HTTP(S)_PROXY` variables in the run's environment route there; Python's
`urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, the Anthropic SDK and Node's `fetch` pick them up automatically. Chromium is
already configured. Setup (`uv sync`, `npm ci`, …) has network, but nothing it starts survives into the
run.

## Event details

- The event is on 10 October 2026.
- A team has up to five people.
- A scored run has 20 minutes on the clock; a test run has up to 2 hours.
- Ask the organizers about the submission deadline and prizes.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).

---

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

1	# Prepare a tender response
2	
3	You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.
4	
5	Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.
6	
7	## Rules
8	
9	1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
10	2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
11	3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
12	4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
13	5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
14	6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
15	7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
16	8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.
17	
18	
19	## Additional rules
20	
21	These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.
22	
23	- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
24	- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
25	- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
26	- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
27	- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
28	- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
29	- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
30	- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
31	- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
32	- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
33	- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
34	- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
35	- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
36	- Currency: the valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
37	- Packaging: Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
38	- Delivery: Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
39	- Shared setup: Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
40	- Project bonus: the finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
41	- Final price: clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
42	- Metal indices: select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
43	- Scoring in bid cases: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.
44	
45	## Site access
46	
47	- tender-portal: https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run
48	  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`
49	- customer-portal: https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run
50	  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`
51	- erp: https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run
52	  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`
53	- mail: https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run
54	  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`
55	
56	## Submission
57	
58	Submit through the tender portal's "Angebotsabgabe" at https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run, after "Teilnahme bekunden" for this tender. Register the bidder using the company name Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH and USt-IdNr. DE811234567. Choose Hauptangebot for bid or Verzichtserklärung for no_bid. Complete the material configurator, enter the discounted net unit prices and total in German number format, and acknowledge the tender documents. The displayed gross amount includes VAT and is not the required net total. Retrieve the signing TAN from the bidder's webmail, review the summary, and confirm "Angebot verbindlich abgeben" in the browser dialog.
59	
60	Exactly one submission is allowed; submitting ends the run. Wall-clock time and LLM tokens count toward your result. Unsaved entries are lost when the portal session expires. Going back clears the later steps. A new TAN request invalidates the previous TAN; each TAN is valid for five minutes.

# Prepare a tender response

You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
- Currency: the valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
- Packaging: Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
- Delivery: Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
- Shared setup: Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
- Project bonus: the finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
- Final price: clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
- Metal indices: select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
- Scoring in bid cases: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

Submit through the tender portal's "Angebotsabgabe" at https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run, after "Teilnahme bekunden" for this tender. Register the bidder using the company name Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH and USt-IdNr. DE811234567. Choose Hauptangebot for bid or Verzichtserklärung for no_bid. Based on the search results, I can provide you with information about Cloudflare's Clef decision model announcement:

## Cloudflare Clef Decision Model

Cloudflare announced Clef and Clef-flash as open-source decision models on October 1, 2026, during their Birthday Week.

### The Three Question Types

Clef features three response types: noul (a probability from 0 to 1), choice (probabilities and confidence for multiple options), and score (probability-weighted levels on an ordered scale). More specifically:

- Noul is for true/false judgments, choice is for selecting among named candidates, and score is for rating ordered levels
- A Score places data on an ordered scale of 2 to 10 levels you describe, lowest first, and returns a probability-weighted level that can land between two of them

### How It Works

Clef is Cloudflare's 27-billion-parameter model for typed decisions. Cloudflare built Clef on top of Qwen, Alibaba's open model family, with Clef starting from Qwen3.8-27B and Clef-flash from Qwen3.5-9B.

Unlike traditional LLMs, Clef uses Qwen to process the entire input and then evaluates the permitted options in parallel with a dedicated mechanism, deriving the probability of each option directly from internal information rather than generating rationale as text.

Based on the search results, here's the current status of WebMCP in 2026:

## What is WebMCP?

WebMCP (Web Model Context Protocol) is a browser-native JavaScript API that lets websites expose structured, callable tools to AI agents operating inside a user's active browser session.

## Current API Status

The API moved from navigator.modelContext to document.modelContext mid-2026, Chrome is running an origin trial through version 156, and almost every tutorial online still shows the deprecated call. WebMCP is currently in experimental stage, and early discussions may have referenced navigator.modelContext, but Chrome documentation now uses document.modelContext.

## Standardization Status

It is a W3C Draft Community Group Report (last published 26 August 2026), not a ratified standard. It is developed in the W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group, edited by engineers from Google and Microsoft.

## Browser Support

Chrome runs a public origin trial from version 149 through 156. Edge is behind a flag. Firefox and Safari have not committed.

## How It Works

WebMCP is a proposed web API that lets a page hand its own functions to an AI agent running in the browser. You call registerTool() and the agent can now invoke that JavaScript function.

Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive overview of web agent perception methods in 2026:

## Accessibility Tree vs. Screenshot vs. Code Generation

### Token Cost Comparison

Playwright MCP streams accessibility snapshots at 114K tokens per task, while Playwright CLI achieves the same job for 27K tokens. More broadly, accessibility snapshots use ~120 tokens compared to ~1,500 tokens for full-page screenshots—roughly 12x cheaper.

### How Accessibility Trees Work

Playwright MCP reads the browser's accessibility tree instead of taking screenshots, giving AI agents a structured, token-efficient view of any web page. When Playwright MCP captures a page, it reads the browser's accessibility tree—the same semantic structure screen readers use—including element roles, names, and stable reference IDs.

### Reliability and Perception Approaches

The agent reads a compact text representation and acts on elements by reference, consuming roughly a quarter of the tokens a screenshot-based approach would need. However, accessibility trees were built for screen readers, not AI agents, and on 95.9% of the web's top million pages, the underlying markup has detectable failures that agents inherit.

### Hybrid Approaches in Production

Combining accessibility tree snapshots with selective vision achieved ~85% success on the WebGames benchmark, compared to ~50% for prior browser agents. Perplexity's Comet uses Chrome's accessibility tree with element reference IDs, falling back to vision selectively.

### Playwright CLI vs. MCP

In Playwright CLI, snapshots are written to disk rather than streamed into context, with agents receiving a file path instead of full accessibility trees, significantly reducing token overhead.

Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive overview of web browsing agent architectures in 2026:

## Key Players and Architectures

Three paradigms dominate: code-as-action (Webwright), DOM-snapshot (Browser-Use), and hybrid NL+code (Stagehand).

**Webwright (Microsoft Research):** Instead of predicting coordinates or selecting DOM elements, it generates executable Playwright Python scripts as its action space. Webwright leads benchmarks with 86.7% Online-Mind2Web and 60.1% Odysseys, outperforming both alternatives by 15+ points on long-horizon tasks.

**Browser-Use:** The leading open-source browser agent framework with 21K+ GitHub stars and an 89% success rate on the WebVoyager benchmark. Browser Use supports multi-tab browsing, persistent memory, and parallel agent execution.

**Stagehand (Browserbase):** An open-source framework for building browser automation agents with natural language, built on Playwright. According to recent leaderboards, Stagehand with Claude Sonnet 4.5 scores 55.0% on Online-Mind2Web.

## Execution Models

Browser Use is agent-first built around a Python library where you provide a goal in natural language, and the system enters a reasoning loop, observing the page, determining the next action, executing it, and reassessing state, with each meaningful step depending on live LLM inference.

## Online Mind2Web Leaderboard

Online Mind2Web is the live, online version of Mind2Web that does not rely on cached pages and allows real-time testing against dynamic and evolving web interfaces. 22 evaluations used two task-specific agent scaffolds (SeeAct and Browser-Use) and 12 different language models.

# Architecture options for the RFQ agent

Research note, 10 Oct 2026. Sources: the platform docs (`/start.md`, `/challenges/rfq.md`, `/llms-full.txt`), the
public run brief (`GET /v1/challenges/rfq/scouting`), and a light look at how the four scouting sites behave. No
scenario value (reference, material, price, login, label) is recorded here, and none may enter `agent/`.

## 1. What the problem statement actually asks for

One signed bid for one tender, assembled from four German business sites, entered in the tender portal's
configurator and signed with a TAN from the webmail. The answer goes in **on the site**, not through the API.

| Fact | Consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Order: eligible, then quality 0 to 100, then cost x time | Cost and time are only a tie-break. Correctness is the game. |
| Eligible = right tender reference in a **signed** submission | A run that never signs scores 0. Signing reliably is step one. |
| Exactly one submission, it ends the run | No "submit early, improve later". The agent needs a deadline-driven best answer. |
| 20 min scored run, TAN valid 5 min, going back clears later steps | Form entry is a transaction: have all values ready before starting it. |
| Money compared to the cent, 29 rules define one answer | Arithmetic must be deterministic code (Decimal, HALF_UP), never model output. |
| Final run = our **latest passed** submission on a private set | Every `atira submit` replaces the finalist. A worse later submit is a real loss. |
| Private set: same jobs, rules and schema; other software, layout, navigation, site names, data, and a different split of information across sites | Anything keyed on URL, selector, label, siteId or click order is worth zero there. |
| AI reviewer rejects fixed click paths, crawlers, copied values | The model must pick targets, searches and documents. Helpers may parse, paginate, calculate, validate, retry, fill. |
| Leaderboard today: best 21.5, most teams 0 or ineligible | Nobody has it. A correct, signed, partially right bid already ranks near the top. |

What stays constant between public and private, and is therefore safe to build on:

- the 29 rules and the scoring weights (the brief restates them in every run);
- the answer schema;
- the four job roles (tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, webmail) and the German domain vocabulary of the rules;
- the adversarial style: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, session timeouts, look-alike and
  superseded records, iframes and ZIPs, self-closing popups, paging, mixed time zones.

What does not stay constant: everything about how a site is built and where a fact lives.

Observed site behaviour that matters for design (behaviour, not content):

- Server-rendered pages, small (roughly 1 to 2 k characters of visible text). Reading as text is cheap.
- Identifiers are rendered with invisible characters between the letters, so naive string matching and regexes on
  page text fail. Text must be normalised; a screenshot is unaffected.
- Decoy UI drawn inside the page (fake browser bars, download prompts, notices). A text dump mixes it with content.
- At least one pointer-drag "unlock" widget. HTTP-only access cannot pass it; real pointer events are needed.
- Message bodies sit in lazy iframes; some content is behind a dialog or an explicit "request access" step.
- Random 503 pages with a retry link; each site reports times in a different zone.

So the task is four problems, not one: **(a)** find evidence on hostile sites, **(b)** decide which of several
competing records governs (exact reference, authorised sender, latest date not after the scenario date),
**(c)** exact arithmetic, **(d)** a long stateful form with a second-factor step. Browsing frameworks only address
(a) and (d). Most of the 100 points are lost in (b) and (c).

## 2. Overfit, underfit, and where the line is

- **Overfit** (dies on the private set, and the reviewer rejects it): selectors, URL paths, page labels, transaction
  codes, click sequences, `if site_id == ...`, prompt text that describes the public sites, few-shot examples copied
  from them, tuning until public-1 scores well.
- **Underfit** (what most of the leaderboard is doing): a generic "browse and figure it out" agent with no domain
  structure. It gets lost, burns the 20 minutes, and does arithmetic in its head.
- **Target: domain-typed, site-agnostic.** Encode what the rules guarantee (evidence schema, authority and time
  resolution, the calculator, the answer schema). Leave everything about the sites to the model at run time.

Rule of thumb for any line of code or prompt: *would it still be true on a site we have never seen?* The rules pass
that test. A label seen on public-1 does not, unless the brief itself states it (then read it from the brief at run
time rather than typing it into code).

## 3. The design space (axes)

Every web agent in use today is one choice per axis. "All combinations" is this table.

### A. What the model sees

| # | Option | Used by | Fit here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Cleaned text / markdown of the page | reader tools, most RAG scrapers | Cheap, exact digits. Polluted by decoys and invisible characters; needs normalising. |
| A2 | Accessibility tree with element refs | Playwright MCP, browser-use, Comet | Good default: compact, actionable. Depends on site markup quality. |
| A3 | Screenshot only | Claude computer use, OpenAI CUA, Gemini computer use, UI-TARS | Immune to DOM tricks, handles drag widgets. Slow, costly, risky for cent-exact numbers. |
| A4 | Screenshot with numbered marks (Set-of-Marks) | WebVoyager, SeeAct | Middle ground; grounding is easier than raw coordinates. |
| A5 | **Hybrid: text first, screenshot on demand or when stuck** | Stagehand, Comet, most 2026 production agents | Best fit. Text for reading numbers, pixels for layout, decoys and widgets. |
| A6 | Network level: HTML or JSON over the browser's own session | "API-first" agents | Fast for reading. Cannot do pointer widgets; looks like a crawler if code picks the URLs. |
| A7 | Document parsers (PDF, ZIP, iframe) | everywhere | Required helper, explicitly allowed for a document the model chose. |

### B. How the model acts

| # | Option | Used by | Fit here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | Fixed primitive tools: click(ref), type, select, goto, back | browser-use, Playwright MCP | Reliable, many small steps, each one a model call. |
| B2 | Mouse and keyboard at coordinates | computer-use models | Needed only for pointer widgets and native dialogs. |
| B3 | Natural-language atomic actions with self-healing: act / extract / observe | Stagehand | Good ergonomics; one extra model call per action. |
| B4 | **Code as action**: the model writes a short Playwright snippet that runs in a guarded REPL | Webwright (MSR), CodeAct, smolagents | Several steps per model call, loops over rows for free. Strong on long tasks. |
| B5 | HTTP as action: the model issues a GET or a form POST through the browser context | hybrid API/browse agents | Fast reads on server-rendered sites; brittle on anything stateful. |
| B6 | Semantic tools built generically on B1: search(query), open(result), read_document(link), fill_form(mapping) | most in-house agents | Fewer steps, still site-agnostic if implemented from the live DOM, not from known selectors. |
| B7 | Site-declared tools (WebMCP, OpenAPI, llms.txt) | emerging | Not offered by these sites. Cheap to probe for; see section 8. |

### C. Who decides (control)

| # | Option | Used by | Fit here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | One ReAct loop | baseline everywhere | Context fills up, serial, slow. The 0 to 21 point results look like this. |
| C2 | Planner then executor | Agent-E, plan-and-act | Good, but the plan must change as Q&A reveals new keys. |
| C3 | **Lead plus parallel workers, each with its own context and browser** | Magentic-One, Anthropic's research pattern | Natural fit for 4 browsers. Workers return findings, not transcripts. |
| C4 | **Shared evidence ledger (blackboard)** | Magentic-One ledgers | Needed: tender Q&A yields keys that the mail and ERP searches depend on. |
| C5 | Staged graph with agentic stages | LangGraph-style | Good outer skeleton: discover, gather, resolve, calculate, enter, sign. |
| C6 | Redundant workers plus voting | self-consistency, debate | Nearly free in wall-clock with 32 concurrent Qwen calls. Use on high-value facts. |
| C7 | Independent verifier | generator plus critic | High value: every fact used is re-checked against its quoted source. |
| C8 | **Skill induction inside the run**: the model works one item by hand, then writes its own routine for the rest | Agent Workflow Memory, SkillWeaver, Voyager | Script speed without a shipped script. Generalises because the routine is authored against the site it finds. |
| C9 | Tree search with backtracking | LATS | Too slow, and form steps are not reversible. Read-only exploration at most. |

### D. Who computes

| # | Option | Fit here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Model does the arithmetic | No. Rounding order alone guarantees cent errors. |
| D2 | **Model extracts typed facts, deterministic code calculates** | Yes. The rules are fixed for both datasets, so this is the most general asset we can build. |
| D3 | Model turns rule prose into parameters (which clause, which allocation rule) | Needed where a mail states the rule in prose. Output is an enum or a small structured spec, then D2 runs it. |
| D4 | Model writes calculation code per run | Fallback for a rule variant D2 does not cover. |

### E. Which model does what

| # | Mix | Cost per run (rough) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | Qwen for everything | about $0.1 to 0.5 | No key needed. 256k context, tools, vision. Weakest link is multi-rule reasoning; D2 and C7 take that load off it. |
| E2 | Qwen workers, **Clef as gate** | adds cents | Clef returns calibrated probabilities for typed questions: "is this the current revision", "does this mail name exactly this reference", "which of these links". Good as verifier and as an abstain signal. Not a reader or planner. |
| E3 | Qwen workers, frontier lead and auditor (own key) | dollars | A handful of frontier calls for the plan, conflict resolution and the final audit. Best quality per dollar if we have a key. |
| E4 | Frontier everywhere | several dollars or more | Highest ceiling, slowest to tie-break. Only sensible because quality outranks cost. |
| E5 | Qwen for reading, a computer-use model for pointer widgets | small | Only if Qwen's own grounding fails on drag widgets. Test Qwen first; it is strong on GUI benchmarks. |
| E6 | Qwen x3 voting, disagreement escalates to Clef or frontier | small | Turns free concurrency into accuracy. |

Cost is a tie-break behind quality, so a mix should be chosen for correctness and variance first.

## 4. Named combinations

| # | Combination | Generalises | Quality ceiling | Time | Review risk | Build effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | browser-use or Stagehand loop, one model (A2, B1/B3, C1, D1) | Medium | Low | Slow | None | Lowest |
| 2 | Pure computer use, frontier model (A3, B2, C1, D1) | High for navigation | Low to medium | Slowest | None | Low |
| 3 | Fixed pipeline with scripted paths, model for extraction only | None | High on public only | Fast | **Rejected** | Medium |
| 4 | HTTP crawl of all sites, then one large model call | Low | Medium | Fast | **Rejected** (crawler) | Low |
| 5 | Lead plus 4 site workers, shared ledger, deterministic calculator (A5, B1+B6, C3+C4+C5, D2) | High | High | Medium | None | Medium |
| 6 | Combination 5 with code-as-action and in-run skill induction (B4, C8) | High | High | Fast | Low, if the model authors the code at run time | Medium to high |
| 7 | Combination 5 or 6 with voting and an independent verifier (C6, C7, Clef gate) | High | Highest | Medium | None | Higher |
| 8 | Combination 7 with a frontier lead and auditor (E3) | High | Highest | Medium | None | Same, needs a key |

Combinations 1 and 2 are where the field is, and why scores are low. 3 and 4 are the tempting shortcuts that the
rules exist to stop, and both fail on the private set anyway.

## 5. Recommendation

Build **5 first, grow it into 7**, on Qwen with Clef as a gate (E2 then E6). Add 6 (code as action) only after 5
signs a bid end to end. Move to 8 only if a frontier key is available and test runs show the remaining errors are
reasoning errors rather than retrieval errors.

```
brief ──> Lead (reads rules, writes the fact plan, owns the clock)
             │  questions                        ▲  typed findings + source quote
   ┌─────────┼─────────┬─────────┐               │
 Worker    Worker    Worker    Worker     one per browser; role found by looking, not by siteId
   └─────────┴────┬────┴─────────┘
            Evidence ledger   {key, value, unit, reference, sender, date, source, quote}
                  │
            Resolver (code)   exact reference, authorised sender, latest date <= scenario date
                  │
            Calculator (code) Decimal, HALF_UP at the steps the rules name, self-checking
                  │
            Verifier          re-reads each used fact against its quote; Clef or second pass
                  │
            Submitter         generic form agent: fill, TAN, review, sign; starts at a fixed time budget
```

Why this shape generalises:

- The only fixed knowledge is the rules. Workers get a **question** ("which price condition is valid on this date
  for this material, with all scales"), never a path.
- Site roles are discovered: each worker opens its site and reports what it holds. If the private set moves a fact
  to another site, the lead re-routes the question. Nothing branches on a site name.
- The model selects records; code only applies the tie-break the rule states. That split is exactly what the
  fair-play rules allow ("calculate, validate"), and it removes the most common reasoning error.
- One generic form filler serves any configurator: read the live form, map answer fields to inputs, write, re-read,
  confirm. German number formatting is a formatter, not a prompt instruction.

Build order, by points and by how well each step transfers:

1. **Signed submission with the right reference and decision.** Eligibility plus 10 points, and it beats most of the
   board. Includes the TAN flow and the deadline guard (begin entry with a fixed margin, submit by about T minus 90 s,
   use "omit position" for anything unfinished).
2. **Material and quantity per position** (35 % of position points): current revision, scoped amendments, Q&A
   quantity changes and withdrawals, unit conversion, exact attribute match, the no-bid decision.
3. **Base price, discount, lead time, total**: validity window, scale, currency, conditional approval, pooled stock.
4. **Surcharge, packaging, bonus, setup pool, metal index**: each is independent credit; add one at a time.

## 6. Measuring generalisation with one public scenario

We cannot see the private set, so we manufacture distribution shift locally.

- **Blind roles:** in local runs, shuffle site order and replace every `siteId` with an opaque token.

One signed bid for one tender, assembled from four German business sites, entered in the tender portal's
configurator and signed with a TAN from the webmail. The answer goes in **on the site**, not through the API.

| Fact | Consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Order: eligible, then quality 0 to 100, then cost x time | Cost and time are only a tie-break. Correctness is the game. |
| Eligible = right tender reference in a **signed** submission | A run that never signs scores 0. Signing reliably is step one. |
| Exactly one submission, it ends the run | No "submit early, improve later". The agent needs a deadline-driven best answer. |
| 20 min scored run, TAN valid 5 min, going back clears later steps | Form entry is a transaction: have all values ready before starting it. |
| Money compared to the cent, 29 rules define one answer | Arithmetic must be deterministic code (Decimal, HALF_UP), never model output. |
| Final run = our **latest passed** submission on a private set | Every `atira submit` replaces the finalist. A worse later submit is a real loss. |

| AI reviewer rejects fixed click paths, crawlers, copied values | The model must pick targets, searches and documents. Helpers may parse, paginate, calculate, validate, retry, fill. |
| Leaderboard today: best 21.5, most teams 0 or ineligible | Nobody has it. A correct, signed, partially right bid already ranks near the top. |

What stays constant between public and private, and is therefore safe to build on:

- the 29 rules and the scoring weights (the brief restates them in every run);
- the answer schema;
- the four job roles (tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, webmail) and the German domain vocabulary of the rules;
- the adversarial style: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, session timeouts, look-alike and
  superseded records, iframes and ZIPs, self-closing popups, paging, mixed time zones.

What does not stay constant: everything about how a site is built and where a fact lives.

Observed site behaviour that matters for design (behaviour, not content):

- Server-rendered pages, small (roughly 1 to 2 k characters of visible text). Reading as text is cheap.
- Identifiers are rendered with invisible characters between the letters, so naive string matching and regexes on
  page text fail. Text must be normalised; a screenshot is unaffected.
- Decoy UI drawn inside the page (fake browser bars, download prompts, notices). A text dump mixes it with content.
- At least one pointer-drag "unlock" widget. HTTP-only access cannot pass it; real pointer events are needed.
- Message bodies sit in lazy iframes; some content is behind a dialog or an explicit "request access" step.
- Random 503 pages with a retry link; each site reports times in a different zone.

So the task is four problems, not one: **(a)** find evidence on hostile sites, **(b)** decide which of several
competing records governs (exact reference, authorised sender, latest date not after the scenario date),
**(c)** exact arithmetic, **(d)** a long stateful form with a second-factor step. Browsing frameworks only address
(a) and (d). Most of the 100 points are lost in (b) and (c).

## 2. Overfit, underfit, and where the line is

- **Overfit** (dies on the private set, and the reviewer rejects it): selectors, URL paths, page labels, transaction
  codes, click sequences, `if site_id == ...`, prompt text that describes the public sites, few-shot examples copied
  from them, tuning until public-1 scores well.
- **Underfit** (what most of the leaderboard is doing): a generic "browse and figure it out" agent with no domain
  structure. It gets lost, burns the 20 minutes, and does arithmetic in its head.
- **Target: domain-typed, site-agnostic.** Encode what the rules guarantee (evidence schema, authority and time
  resolution, the calculator, the answer schema). Leave everything about the sites to the model at run time.

Rule of thumb for any line of code or prompt: *would it still be true on a site we have never seen?* The rules pass
that test. A label seen on public-1 does not, unless the brief itself states it (then read it from the brief at run
time rather than typing it into code).

## 3. The design space (axes)

Every web agent in use today is one choice per axis. "All combinations" is this table.

### A. What the model sees

| # | Option | Used by | Fit here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Cleaned text / markdown of the page | reader tools, most RAG scrapers | Cheap, exact digits. Polluted by decoys and invisible characters; needs normalising. |
| A2 | Accessibility tree with element refs | Playwright MCP, browser-use, Comet | Good default: compact, actionable. Depends on site markup quality. |
| A3 | Screenshot only | Claude computer use, OpenAI CUA, Gemini computer use, UI-TARS | Immune to DOM tricks, handles drag widgets. Slow, costly, risky for cent-exact numbers. |

| A5 | **Hybrid: text first, screenshot on demand or when stuck** | Stagehand, Comet, most 2026 production agents | Best fit. Text for reading numbers, pixels for layout, decoys and widgets. |
| A6 | Network level: HTML or JSON over the browser's own session | "API-first" agents | Fast for reading. Cannot do pointer widgets; looks like a crawler if code picks the URLs. |
| A7 | Document parsers (PDF, ZIP, iframe) | everywhere | Required helper, explicitly allowed for a document the model chose. |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| D4 | Model writes calculation code per run | Fallback for a rule variant D2 does not cover. |

| # | Mix | Cost per run (rough) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | Qwen for everything | about $0.1 to 0.5 | No key needed. 256k context, tools, vision. Weakest link is multi-rule reasoning; D2 and C7 take that load off it. |

| E6 | Qwen x3 voting, disagreement escalates to Clef or frontier | small | Turns free concurrency into accuracy. |
