1	# Getting started: from sign-in to your first scored run
2	
3	How to sign in, set up and test your agent, and get it on the leaderboard. Limits and scoring are at the bottom.
4	
5	Fastest start: point Claude Code or Codex at this site. Paste this, and it installs the CLI, connects itself, and helps you build, test and submit:
6	
7	```text
8	Read https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt, then set us up and help us build, test and submit an agent for this challenge.
9	```
10	
11	Web page: [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start) · The challenge: [Markdown](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md) · For agents: [llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt) · [OpenAPI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json) · [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) · [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)
12	
13	## What you're building
14	
15	Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid. Bring any frontier model, your own tools and prompts, up to four browsers in parallel; no human in the loop. Or use [ours](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models): unlimited Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef inference. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. Every scored submission runs once on the public dataset. Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
16	
17	## Your first test run
18	
19	Seven steps. The first five get your agent running against the websites. Step 6 tests it in the sandbox; step 7 puts it on the leaderboard.
20	
21	### 1. Sign in and form a team
22	
23	[Sign in with GitHub](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/login?next=/team) and create a team of up to 5. Invite teammates by their GitHub username on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); each invite works only for that account.
24	
25	### 2. Install the CLI and sign in
26	
27	The [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) is one file for Node 24; where Node 24 is missing, the installer offers a private copy for atira alone. `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a token for this computer. On macOS and Linux, the second line puts `atira` on your PATH in this terminal; add it to your shell's startup file to keep it. Optional: connect your coding agent ([MCP](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)), and it starts test runs, reads logs and sees each browser's screen itself. Or skip the install: point a coding agent at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt).
28	
29	macOS and Linux:
30	
31	```sh
32	curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh
33	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
34	atira login
35	```
36	
37	Windows, in PowerShell:
38	
39	```powershell
40	irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex
41	atira login
42	```
43	
44	Optional: connect the coding agent you use (one line each):
45	
46	```sh
47	claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
48	codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
49	```
50	
51	### 3. Scout the websites yourself
52	
53	Logins for every website, with the public data. Click around as much as you like. None of it is scored. Rules at a glance: [Fair play](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md)
54	
55	| Website | URL | Username | Password |
56	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
57	| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `uJC8-80QSb7rblI_k4tH` |
58	| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `k2sBynnldp0mqU4MviqI` |
59	| ERP | <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `vuUcG2MsDEafLhoMjfS5` |
60	| Webmail (Werkpost) | <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `ldPxYRdvI__aVKKqOWIy` |
61	
62	### 4. Choose your starting point
63	
64	Fork the starter kit, or build your own from the [run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md) in any language, framework or architecture. The kit is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and submits an answer (`run.py`), attaches to the run's browsers (`browsers.py`), shows one call to each hosted model (`models.py`), and leaves your agent to `solve()` in `agent.py`.
65	
66	macOS and Linux:
67	
68	```sh
69	mkdir my-agent
70	curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz | tar xz -C my-agent
71	```
72	
73	Windows, in PowerShell:
74	
75	```powershell
76	mkdir my-agent
77	curl.exe -fsSL -o starter-kit.tar.gz https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz
78	tar -xzf starter-kit.tar.gz -C my-agent
79	```
80	
81	### 5. Develop locally
82	
83	You need uv for the starter kit ([install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with `atira models proxy` and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. `atira scout --env` gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, `atira test-run` runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: [how a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md).
84	
85	macOS and Linux:
86	
87	```sh
88	cd my-agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
89	eval "$(atira scout --env)"
90	uv run --no-sync python agent.py
91	```
92	
93	Windows, in PowerShell:
94	
95	```powershell
96	cd my-agent; uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
97	atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
98	uv run --no-sync python agent.py
99	```
100	
101	Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: [how to call them](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models).
102	
103	### 6. Test in the sandbox
104	
105	The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); only the timed run step gets it.
106	
107	```sh
108	atira test-run .
109	```
110	
111	### 7. Submit
112	
113	A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard). One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. [Submitting in full](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md).
114	
115	```sh
116	atira submit .
117	```
118	
119	## Unlimited Inference
120	
121	We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
122	
123	### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
124	
125	#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.
126	
127	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
128	- **Simulated pricing:**
129	  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
130	  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
131	  - Cache writes: Free
132	  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
133	- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)
134	
135	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
136	
137	```python
138	import os
139	from openai import OpenAI
140	
141	qwen = OpenAI(
142	    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
143	    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
144	)
145	reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
146	    model="qwen",
147	    messages=[{
148	        "role": "user",
149	        "content": "Which button submits?",
150	    }],
151	)
152	```
153	
154	### Cloudflare Clef
155	
156	A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.
157	
158	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
159	- **Simulated pricing:**
160	  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
161	  - Output: Not priced
162	
163	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
164	
165	```sh
166	curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
167	  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
168	  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
169	  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
170	  "questions": {"next": {
171	    "type": "choice",
172	    "instructions": "What next?",
173	    "criteria": {
174	      "retry": "Retry the request",
175	      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
176	```
177	
178	In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.
179	
180	```sh
181	atira login   # once per computer
182	atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
183	export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
184	export QWEN_API_KEY=local
185	export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
186	export CLEF_API_KEY=local
187	```
188	
189	Cost and time count toward your rank, and a call to these models costs a fraction of a frontier call. Use them for the easy steps.
190	
191	If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.
192	
193	## Limits
194	
195	What every scored run gets.
196	
197	| Rule | What it means |
198	| --- | --- |
199	| Scored run | 20 minutes on the clock. Each submission runs once; one submission in flight per team. |
200	| Setup and network | Setup doesn't count toward your time: it has network access and up to 5 minutes to install what you need. The timed run reaches only the platform, the websites and the model proxy. |
201	| Models | Bring your own keys as team secrets, for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. |
202	| Browsers | At most 4 Chromium browsers at a time, provided by the sandbox; any number of tabs. |
203	| Sandbox | 4 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 30 GB disk on AMD Zen 5; 1280×800 screens. Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, Rust with cargo. |
204	| Package | Up to 20 MB compressed, with `agent.json` at the root. Its `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls (`["qwen", "clef"]` when absent); the run waits only for those to warm up, and `"models": []` starts it right after setup. |
205	| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
206	| Team | Up to 5 people. |
207	
208	## How you're scored
209	
210	Every scored run gets a quality and an eligibility verdict; the platform measures its cost and time.
211	
212	- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
213	- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.
214	
215	Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.
216	
217	Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.
218	
219	On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.
220	
221	## Public and private data
222	
223	The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too. When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
224	
225	## Using a coding agent?
226	
227	Point it at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt); the home page, Getting started, each challenge, its leaderboard and each team's profile are also Markdown (add `.md` to the URL, `/index.md` for the home page), the API is described in [openapi.json](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json), and the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) shows every call with curl.
228	
229	Or plug the CLI in as an MCP server: your agent lists your runs, queries their logs by time, sees a browser's screen at any moment, starts test runs and, once you confirm, submits. [Debug runs from your coding agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md) has the tools and other clients.
230	
231	```sh
232	claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
233	codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
234	```


### 5. Develop locally

You need uv for the starter kit ([install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with `atira models proxy` and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. `atira scout --env` gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, `atira test-run` runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: [how a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md).

macOS and Linux:

```sh
cd my-agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
cd my-agent; uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: [how to call them](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models).

### 6. Test in the sandbox

The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); only the timed run step gets it.

```sh
atira test-run .
```

### 7. Submit

A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard). One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. [Submitting in full](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md).

```sh
atira submit .
```

## Unlimited Inference

We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.

### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
  - Cache writes: Free
  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

qwen = OpenAI(
    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
)
reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen",
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Which button submits?",
    }],
)
```

### Cloudflare Clef

A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
  - Output: Not priced

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

```sh
curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
  "questions": {"next": {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": "What next?",
    "criteria": {
      "retry": "Retry the request",
      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
```

In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.

```sh
atira login   # once per computer
atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
export QWEN_API_KEY=local
export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
export CLEF_API_KEY=local
```

Cost and time count toward your rank, and a call to these models costs a fraction of a frontier call. Use them for the easy steps.

If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.

## Limits

What every scored run gets.

| Rule | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Scored run | 20 minutes on the clock. Each submission runs once; one submission in flight per team. |
| Setup and network | Setup doesn't count toward your time: it has network access and up to 5 minutes to install what you need. The timed run reaches only the platform, the websites and the model proxy. |
| Models | Bring your own keys as team secrets, for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. |
| Browsers | At most 4 Chromium browsers at a time, provided by the sandbox; any number of tabs. |
| Sandbox | 4 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 30 GB disk on AMD Zen 5; 1280×800 screens. Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, Rust with cargo. |
| Package | Up to 20 MB compressed, with `agent.json` at the root. Its `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls (`["qwen", "clef"]` when absent); the run waits only for those to warm up, and `"models": []` starts it right after setup. |
| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
| Team | Up to 5 people. |

## How you're scored

Every scored run gets a quality and an eligibility verdict; the platform measures its cost and time.

- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.

Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.

Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.

On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.

## Public and private data

The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too. When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

## Using a coding agent?

Point it at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt); the home page, Getting started, each challenge, its leaderboard and each team's profile are also Markdown (add `.md` to the URL, `/index.md` for the home page), the API is described in [openapi.json](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json), and the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) shows every call with curl.

Or plug the CLI in as an MCP server: your agent lists your runs, queries their logs by time, sees a browser's screen at any moment, starts test runs and, once you confirm, submits. [Debug runs from your coding agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md) has the tools and other clients.

```sh
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
```

content.text:
The run is still going (about 5 minutes in, 217 model calls, $0.10 so far). The platform returned a 503 to my log follower, so I've reattached it; the run itself wasn't affected.

## How this run differs from the team's earlier ones

The earlier runs (v1) read the brief, opened the tender portal, marked every position as omitted and signed. That is eligible but scores only the 10 points for decision and reference, in about 2.5 minutes for $0.011.

This run (v2) tries to earn the other 90 points by actually pricing the bid:

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `research.py` (new) | Workers browse the four sites in three stages and keep the pages that matter |
| `evidence.py` (new) | A model call copies records (positions, materials, price conditions, mails) off the kept pages, checked against the page text |
| `bidplan.py`, `parse.py` (new) | Code decides which record governs, parses numbers and dates, and feeds the team's existing `calc.py` |
| `submit.py` | Enters the priced positions in the form instead of omitting all of them; a second timed attempt signs whatever the form holds |
| `agent.py`, `browser_tools.py` | Wires the stages together, adds the page-keeping tools, 4 browsers instead of 1 |

## What the live run already shows

- **Working:** the positions were read correctly off the tender portal, and the mail records (logistics, technical release, discount approval) came back with senders, dates and references.
- **Failing:** the supplier-portal worker timed out after 163 seconds, so the specification came back empty. Without the spec no material can be matched, so most position points are probably lost in this run.
- **Suspicious:** the three webmail tabs are redoing the robot check on nearly every step, and one search box received two queries glued together. Several tabs on one login look like they interfere with each other.
- **Expensive:** $0.10 after 5 minutes is already more than the top team's whole run.

## What the teams with 100 did, as far as the public data shows

I can't see their code, only cost and time:

| Team | Runs | Cost | Time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| isar-labs | 100, 100, 100, then 10 on their latest | $0.07 to $0.10 | 6 to 12 min |
| AdminRights | 100 on their first and only submission | $0.24 | 18 min |

Both costs are in the range of a few hundred thousand to a million-plus Qwen tokens, so most likely hosted Qwen and nothing exotic. AdminRights getting 100 on the first try at 18 minutes looks like a plain, patient agent that reads everything in order and lets code do the arithmetic. isar-labs dropping from 100 to 10 with their latest submission shows how much run-to-run variance there is.

## The easiest route to 100, in my view

v2 is more elaborate than it needs to be, and the failures above come from that. The simpler shape:

1. **One agent per site, one login each, no extra tabs.** Each is a plain loop: "find everything about this tender on this site and write it down." That removes the tab interference and the fixed stage timeouts.
2. **One coordinating model that asks the site agents questions in order.** Tender first (positions, Q&A keys), then spec, then ERP, then mail. Later questions depend on earlier answers, and this also survives the private set splitting information differently across sites.
3. **Code does all the maths.** The team's `calc.py` already implements the 29 rules with tests; this is where the exactness comes from.
4. **One agent fills the form and signs.**

On your priorities: eligibility is protected in both versions by the same mechanism (code keeps the clock and signs with the right tender reference even if research produced nothing), and this run will show whether that holds under real conditions. I would not submit anything until a test run both signs and beats 10.

When this run ends I'll give you the score breakdown, then cut v2 down to that simpler shape rather than patch the three-stage version, unless the breakdown says otherwise.

content.thinking: The run scored identically to v1 but cost far more, because the staged multi-tab research design failed to produce a plan in time (spec worker timed out, mail tabs stalled on robot checks, ERP never opened) and eligibility nearly failed too. I'm now rebuilding it as one agent per site logging in simultaneously, including the ERP from the start, with more room for the TAN step.

content.content:
1	"""
2	The investigation: what to find out is fixed by the bid rules, where and how to find it is the model's work.
3	
4	Each lookup is a question to a worker on one website. The worker navigates and keeps the pages that answer it;
5	`evidence.read` copies the records off those pages; `bidplan` decides which record applies and prices the bid.
6	Lookups run side by side in several tabs per website, in the order the rules make one fact depend on another:
7	the tender, its clarifications and the specification first, then the materials, then their prices. The plan is
8	written to `state["plan"]` after every stage, so a bid can be entered from whatever is established when time is up.
9	"""
10	import asyncio
11	import os
12	import time
13	from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
14	from datetime import date
15	from typing import Awaitable, Literal
16	
17	import bidplan
18	import evidence
19	import llm
20	import parse
21	from briefing import Briefing
22	from browser_tools import EVIDENCE_TOOLS, Deps, Kept, SiteSession
23	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
24	from pydantic_ai import Agent, ModelRetry
25	from tracing import Trace
26	from worker import run_worker
27	
28	TABS = int(os.environ.get("AGENT_TABS", "3"))  # workers side by side on one website
29	COLLECT_THINKING = os.environ.get("THINKING_COLLECT") == "1"
30	STAGES = (0.42, 0.72, 1.0)  # share of the research time by which each stage's lookups must be done
31	
32	Role = Literal["discount_approval", "condition_rules", "technical_release", "packaging_tariffs",
33	               "delivery_commitments", "fx_fixing", "setup_pools", "project_bonus", "metal_indices"]
34	
35	ROLES = """\
36	- discount_approval: the sales director's approval of a discount for the tender
37	- condition_rules: the rules that say what the discount applies to for a condition group
38	- technical_release: the release that gives the end reserve for requirements stated as usable travel
39	- packaging_tariffs: the price per carton for a packaging tariff key
40	- delivery_commitments: the committed delivery time for a delivery commitment key
41	- fx_fixing: the exchange rate for an FX key
42	- setup_pools: the fee of a shared setup pool and how it is split
43	- project_bonus: the percentage bands of the project bonus
44	- metal_indices: the rates of the metal price indices"""
45	
46	
47	class Source(BaseModel):
48	    role: Role
49	    subject: str = Field(default="", description="The subject or topic word the brief gives for these messages, "
50	                                                 "exactly as written; '' if it gives none")
51	    sender: str = Field(description="The part before the @ of the sender the brief authorises, exactly as written")
52	
53	
54	class Roles(BaseModel):
55	    """Which website does which job in this run, and whose messages count for what."""
56	    tender_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website with the tender, its positions and bidder Q&A")
57	    spec_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website with the buyer's technical specification")
58	    erp_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website with materials, stock, lead times and prices")
59	    mail_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the bidder's own webmail")
60	    scenario_date: str = Field(description="The scenario date as the brief writes it")
61	    sources: list[Source] = Field(description="One entry per kind of message for which the brief names a sender")
62	
63	
64	def rules_text(task: dict) -> str:
65	    """The brief without the lines that carry this run's logins; workers get it as background."""
66	    secrets = {value for site in task["access"] for value in (site.get("credentials") or {}).values() if value}
67	    return "\n".join(line for line in task["brief"].splitlines() if not any(secret in line for secret in secrets))
68	
69	
70	async def read_roles(task: dict, trace: Trace) -> Roles | None:
71	    """Map the run's websites and the brief's authorised senders to their jobs; None if the model does not manage."""
72	    brief = task["brief"]
73	    ids = {site["siteId"] for site in task["access"]}
74	    agent = Agent(llm.model(timeout=90, max_retries=2), output_type=Roles, model_settings=llm.settings(thinking=True),
75	                  retries=3, instructions="You read a task brief and extract facts from it exactly as written.")
76	
77	    @agent.output_validator
78	    def _from_brief(roles: Roles) -> Roles:
79	        named = {roles.tender_site, roles.spec_site, roles.erp_site, roles.mail_site}
80	        if not named <= ids:
81	            raise ModelRetry(f"The four websites must be among these siteIds: {sorted(ids)}")
82	        text = brief.casefold()
83	        unknown = [value for source in roles.sources for value in (source.subject, source.sender)
84	                   if value and value.casefold() not in text]
85	        if roles.scenario_date not in brief:
86	            unknown.append(roles.scenario_date)
87	        if unknown:
88	            raise ModelRetry(f"{', '.join(unknown)} are not in the brief; copy values exactly from it.")
89	        return roles
90	
91	    sites = "\n".join(f"- siteId {site['siteId']}: {site['url']}" for site in task["access"])
92	    prompt = (f"Websites of this run:\n{sites}\n\nKinds of message the bid rules rely on:\n{ROLES}\n\n"
93	              f"Brief:\n{rules_text(task)}")
94	    try:
95	        roles = (await agent.run(prompt)).output
96	    except Exception as error:
97	        trace.event("roles", "failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}")
98	        return None
99	    trace.event("roles", "done", **roles.model_dump())
100	    return roles
101	
102	
103	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- websites and lookups
104	
105	
106	class Site:
107	    """A website of the run with tabs for several workers; a tab is reused once its worker is done."""
108	
109	    def __init__(self, site: dict, context, trace: Trace, rules: str, tabs: int = TABS):
110	        self.site, self.context, self.trace, self.rules = site, context, trace, rules
111	        self.idle: list[SiteSession] = []
112	        self.opened = 0
113	        self.free = asyncio.Semaphore(tabs)
114	
115	    @asynccontextmanager

159	                             tools=EVIDENCE_TOOLS, deps=deps)

161	            site.trace.event(name, "collected", pages=len(pages), kept=len(deps.kept))

"""
The investigation: what to find out is fixed by the bid rules, where and how to find it is the model's work.

Each lookup is a question to a worker on one website. The worker navigates and keeps the pages that answer it;
`evidence.read` copies the records off those pages; `bidplan` decides which record applies and prices the bid.
Lookups run side by side in several tabs per website, in the order the rules make one fact depend on another:
the tender, its clarifications and the specification first, then the materials, then their prices. The plan is
written to `state["plan"]` after every stage, so a bid can be entered from whatever is established when time is up.
"""
import asyncio
import os
import time
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import date
from typing import Awaitable, Literal

import bidplan
import evidence
import llm
import parse
from briefing import Briefing
from browser_tools import EVIDENCE_TOOLS, Deps, Kept, SiteSession
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic_ai import Agent, ModelRetry
from tracing import Trace
from worker import run_worker

TABS = int(os.environ.get("AGENT_TABS", "3"))  # workers side by side on one website
COLLECT_THINKING = os.environ.get("THINKING_COLLECT") == "1"
STAGES = (0.42, 0.72, 1.0)  # share of the research time by which each stage's lookups must be done

Role = Literal["discount_approval", "condition_rules", "technical_release", "packaging_tariffs",
               "delivery_commitments", "fx_fixing", "setup_pools", "project_bonus", "metal_indices"]

ROLES = """\
- discount_approval: the sales director's approval of a discount for the tender
- condition_rules: the rules that say what the discount applies to for a condition group
- technical_release: the release that gives the end reserve for requirements stated as usable travel
- packaging_tariffs: the price per carton for a packaging tariff key
- delivery_commitments: the committed delivery time for a delivery commitment key
- fx_fixing: the exchange rate for an FX key
- setup_pools: the fee of a shared setup pool and how it is split
- project_bonus: the percentage bands of the project bonus
- metal_indices: the rates of the metal price indices"""


class Source(BaseModel):
    role: Role
    subject: str = Field(default="", description="The subject or topic word the brief gives for these messages, "
                                                 "exactly as written; '' if it gives none")
    sender: str = Field(description="The part before the @ of the sender the brief authorises, exactly as written")


class Roles(BaseModel):
    """Which website does which job in this run, and whose messages count for what."""
    tender_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website with the tender, its positions and bidder Q&A")
    spec_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website with the buyer's technical specification")
    erp_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website with materials, stock, lead times and prices")
    mail_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the bidder's own webmail")
    scenario_date: str = Field(description="The scenario date as the brief writes it")
    sources: list[Source] = Field(description="One entry per kind of message for which the brief names a sender")


def rules_text(task: dict) -> str:
    """The brief without the lines that carry this run's logins; workers get it as background."""
    secrets = {value for site in task["access"] for value in (site.get("credentials") or {}).values() if value}
    return "\n".join(line for line in task["brief"].splitlines() if not any(secret in line for secret in secrets))


async def read_roles(task: dict, trace: Trace) -> Roles | None:
    """Map the run's websites and the brief's authorised senders to their jobs; None if the model does not manage."""
    brief = task["brief"]
    ids = {site["siteId"] for site in task["access"]}
    agent = Agent(llm.model(timeout=90, max_retries=2), output_type=Roles, model_settings=llm.settings(thinking=True),
                  retries=3, instructions="You read a task brief and extract facts from it exactly as written.")

    @agent.output_validator
    def _from_brief(roles: Roles) -> Roles:
        named = {roles.tender_site, roles.spec_site, roles.erp_site, roles.mail_site}
        if not named <= ids:
            raise ModelRetry(f"The four websites must be among these siteIds: {sorted(ids)}")
        text = brief.casefold()
        unknown = [value for source in roles.sources for value in (source.subject, source.sender)
                   if value and value.casefold() not in text]
        if roles.scenario_date not in brief:
            unknown.append(roles.scenario_date)
        if unknown:
            raise ModelRetry(f"{', '.join(unknown)} are not in the brief; copy values exactly from it.")
        return roles

    sites = "\n".join(f"- siteId {site['siteId']}: {site['url']}" for site in task["access"])
    prompt = (f"Websites of this run:\n{sites}\n\nKinds of message the bid rules rely on:\n{ROLES}\n\n"
              f"Brief:\n{rules_text(task)}")
    try:
        roles = (await agent.run(prompt)).output
    except Exception as error:
        trace.event("roles", "failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}")
        return None
    trace.event("roles", "done", **roles.model_dump())
    return roles


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- websites and lookups


class Site:
    """A website of the run with tabs for several workers; a tab is reused once its worker is done."""

    def __init__(self, site: dict, context, trace: Trace, rules: str, tabs: int = TABS):
        self.site, self.context, self.trace, self.rules = site, context, trace, rules
        self.idle: list[SiteSession] = []
        self.opened = 0
        self.free = asyncio.Semaphore(tabs)

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def tab(self):
        async with self.free:
            if self.idle:
                session = self.idle.pop()
            else:
                self.opened += 1
                named = {**self.site, "siteId": f"{self.site['siteId']}/{self.opened}"}
                session = SiteSession(named, self.context, self.trace)
                await session.start()
            try:
                yield session
            finally:
                self.idle.append(session)


KEEP = """

You do not report the facts yourself. Call keep() on every page that shows them, and keep_all_pages(ref) on a list \
or document that continues over several pages; a colleague then reads the kept pages in full. Keep older, superseded \
and look-alike records too when they concern the same thing, so that the right one can be chosen afterwards. Finish \
as soon as everything is kept."""


def _recent(views: list[Kept], limit: int = 12) -> list[Kept]:
    """The last distinct pages a worker looked at, for when it kept none."""
    distinct: dict[str, Kept] = {}
    for view in views:
        distinct.pop(view.text, None)
        distinct[view.text] = view
    return list(distinct.values())[-limit:]


async def collect(site: Site, goal: str, *, name: str, deadline: float, max_steps: int = 30) -> list[Kept]:
    """Have a worker find and keep the pages that answer `goal`; [] when it finds nothing in time."""
    if deadline - time.monotonic() < 20:
        site.trace.event(name, "skipped", reason="no time left")
        return []
    try:
        async with site.tab() as session:
            deps = Deps(session=session)
            first = len(session.views)
            await run_worker(session, goal + KEEP, evidence.Collected, context=site.rules, deadline=deadline,
                             max_steps=max_steps, thinking=COLLECT_THINKING, grounded=False, notes=False,
                             tools=EVIDENCE_TOOLS, deps=deps)
            pages = deps.kept or _recent(session.views[first:])
            site.trace.event(name, "collected", pages=len(pages), kept=len(deps.kept))
            return pages
    except Exception as error:
        site.trace.event(name, "collect_failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}")
        return []


POSITIONS_GOAL = """Find tender {ref} and keep the page or document that lists its positions (the bill of \
quantities): for each position its number, quantity, unit and the specification requirement it refers to. If the \
tender's documents only open after a step such as registering interest in the tender, take that step."""

CLARIFICATIONS_GOAL = """Find the bidder questions and answers (clarifications) of tender {ref} and keep all of them, \
every page, so that each answer's number, date and full text are on a kept page."""

SPEC_GOAL = """Find the buyer's technical specification that belongs to tender {ref}. It exists in several revisions \
and the one shown first may be outdated: find out which revision is marked as the current, valid one, keep the page \
that says so, then open that revision and keep every page of its requirements, so that each requirement's bore, \
stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, catalogue group and pieces per set are on a kept page."""

CANDIDATES_GOAL = """Find the materials of catalogue group {group}. They are needed for:
{wanted}
Keep the result list. Then open the master data of every material that the list does not already rule out by a \
different value, and keep the pages that show its bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification and whether it is \
active or blocked. Keep near misses too, so that it can be checked that they do not fit."""

MATERIAL_GOAL = """Look up material {number}. Keep the pages that show: its stock that is free to sell and any \
blocked stock; its delivery time from stock and its production lead time; its pieces per carton; its allocation mass, \
its surcharge mass and its metal price index; and every one of its price condition records with validity period, \
currency, exchange rate key, price unit and all quantity scales, records of other periods included."""

MAIL_GOAL = """Find the messages about {topic} that concern tender {ref}. Search with the tender reference together \
with a word for the topic, in the inbox and in every other folder (an archive, for example). Open each message \
found and keep it while it is open, so that its sender address, date and full text are on the kept page. Keep older \
messages and ones for similar-looking references as well."""

MAILS_TASK = """List every message that is shown in full (opened), each once: its sender address, its date, the \
tender reference it is about exactly as it writes it, and the keys, codes, groups or revisions it gives values for."""

CONTENT = {
    "condition_rules": (evidence.ConditionRules, "Report what the message rules for each condition group: what the "
                        "order discount applies to."),
    "technical_release": (evidence.Reserves, "Report every end reserve the message releases, with the key or name "
                          "and the specification revision it is for."),
    "packaging_tariffs": (evidence.Tariffs, "Report every packaging tariff of the message with its price per carton."),
    "delivery_commitments": (evidence.Commitments, "Report every delivery commitment of the message: its key, the "
                             "material it is for, the largest quantity it covers and the committed delivery time."),
    "fx_fixing": (evidence.FxRates, "Report every exchange rate of the message and which way it is quoted."),
    "setup_pools": (evidence.Pools, "Report every shared setup pool of the message: its fee and the rule the message "
                    "states for splitting the fee into cents."),
    "project_bonus": (evidence.Bonuses, "Report the project bonus of the message: its percentage bands and what "
                      "value they apply to."),
    "metal_indices": (evidence.Indices, "Report every metal price index of the message with all its rates and the "
                      "period each rate is valid for."),
}


async def _first(task: asyncio.Task | None, default=None):
    """A lookup's result; `default` when it was never started or failed."""
    if task is None:
        return default
    try:
        return await task
    except Exception:
        return default


async def investigate(briefing: Briefing, roles: Roles, sites: dict[str, Site], address: Awaitable[str],
                      trace: Trace, deadline: float, state: dict) -> None:
    """Work out the bid for the briefing's tender by `deadline` (a `time.monotonic()` value) into state["plan"]."""
    try:
        scenario: date = parse.when(roles.scenario_date).date()
    except parse.ParseError:
        trace.event("research", "failed", reason=f"scenario date {roles.scenario_date!r} not readable")
        return
    tender, spec_site, erp, mail = (sites[roles.tender_site], sites[roles.spec_site], sites[roles.erp_site],
                                    sites[roles.mail_site])
    started = time.monotonic()
    stage_one, stage_two, stage_three = (started + (deadline - started) * share for share in STAGES)
    sources = {source.role: source for source in roles.sources}
    notes: list[str] = []
    running: list[asyncio.Task] = []

    def start(lookup) -> asyncio.Task:
        task = asyncio.create_task(lookup)
        running.append(task)
        return task

    try:
        await _stages(briefing, sites_of=(tender, spec_site, erp, mail), sources=sources, scenario=scenario,
                      address=address, trace=trace, started=started, stages=(stage_one, stage_two, stage_three),
                      state=state, notes=notes, start=start)
    finally:  # nothing keeps browsing or calling the model once the bid is being entered
        for task in running:
            task.cancel()


async def _stages(briefing: Briefing, *, sites_of: tuple, sources: dict, scenario: date, address: Awaitable[str],
                  trace: Trace, started: float, stages: tuple[float, float, float], state: dict, notes: list[str],
                  start) -> None:
    ref = briefing.tender_reference
    tender, spec_site, erp, mail = sites_of
    stage_one, stage_two, stage_three = stages

    # ---- stage 1: everything that depends on the tender reference alone

    async def tender_sheet() -> evidence.TenderSheet | None:
        pages = await collect(tender, POSITIONS_GOAL.format(ref=ref), name="positions", deadline=stage_one)
        return await evidence.read(pages, "List every position of the tender's bill of quantities.",
                                   evidence.TenderSheet, trace=trace, name="positions", thinking=False)

    async def spec_sheet() -> evidence.SpecSheet | None:
        pages = await collect(spec_site, SPEC_GOAL.format(ref=ref), name="specification", deadline=stage_one,
                              max_steps=45)
        return await evidence.read(pages, "Report the specification revision that is marked as the current one and "
                                   "every requirement of that revision. If the pages show requirements of several "
                                   "revisions, report only those of the current one.",
                                   evidence.SpecSheet, trace=trace, name="specification")

    async def mails(role: str) -> tuple[list[Kept], list[evidence.Mail]]:
        source = sources[role]
        if role == "discount_approval":
            topic = f"a discount approval by the sales director ({source.sender}@...)"
            listing, task = evidence.Approvals, (MAILS_TASK + " Say for each whether it itself approves a discount "
                                                 "for that reference, with the percentage and any minimum order "
                                                 "value it requires.")
        else:
            topic = repr(source.subject) if source.subject else role.replace("_", " ")
            listing, task = evidence.Mails, MAILS_TASK
        by = stage_three if role in ("fx_fixing", "metal_indices") else stage_two
        pages = await collect(mail, MAIL_GOAL.format(topic=topic, ref=ref), name=role, deadline=by)
        found = await evidence.read(pages, task, listing, trace=trace, name=role, thinking=role == "discount_approval",
                                    context=f"The tender reference being worked on: {ref}")
        return pages, (found.mails if found else [])

    sheet_task = start(tender_sheet())
    clarification_pages = start(
        collect(tender, CLARIFICATIONS_GOAL.format(ref=ref), name="clarifications", deadline=stage_one, max_steps=40))
    spec_task = start(spec_sheet())
    order = ["discount_approval", "technical_release", "condition_rules", "packaging_tariffs", "delivery_commitments",
             "setup_pools", "project_bonus", "fx_fixing", "metal_indices"]
    mail_tasks = {role: start(mails(role)) for role in order if role in sources}

    sheet = await _first(sheet_task)
    if not sheet or not sheet.positions:
        trace.event("research", "failed", reason="the tender's positions were not found")
        return
    spec = await _first(spec_task)
    known = "Tender positions: " + ", ".join(p.position for p in sheet.positions)
    if spec:
        known += (f"\nSpecification revision in force: {spec.revision}\nIts requirements: "
                  + ", ".join(r.requirement for r in spec.requirements))
    clarifications = await evidence.read(
        await _first(clarification_pages, []),
        "List every answer of the tender's bidder questions and answers with what it changes: quantities of "
        "positions, earlier answers it withdraws, technical amendments to a specification revision and requirement, "
        "and what it assigns to positions (a condition group, a packaging tariff key, a delivery commitment key, "
        "membership of a shared setup pool, participation in the project bonus, an ordinary setup fee). Write "
        "position numbers, revisions and requirements the way the known ones are written.",
        evidence.Clarifications, trace=trace, name="clarifications", context=known)
    if clarifications is None:
        notes.append("clarifications not read: tender quantities used, no keys applied")
    if spec is None:
        notes.append("specification not read")
    elif not spec.marked_current:
        notes.append(f"specification revision {spec.revision} not confirmed as current")
    tender_lines = bidplan.lines(sheet, clarifications, spec, scenario, notes)
    revision = spec.revision if spec else ""
    trace.event("research", "stage_one", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1),
                lines=[{"position": line.position, "quantity": line.quantity, "unit": str(line.unit),
                        "attributes": line.attributes, "group": line.group, "keys": line.keys}
                       for line in tender_lines])

    # ---- the bidder's messages: which one governs is decided here, then only that one is read for its content

    mailbox_address = parse.email(await _first(asyncio.ensure_future(address), "") or "")
    domain = mailbox_address.split("@", 1)[1] if "@" in mailbox_address else ""
    records = bidplan.Records()

    async def content(role: str, keys: list[str]) -> list | None:
        """Rule 21 per key: the governing message's records for `role`; None when no message governs."""
        if role not in mail_tasks:
            return None
        pages, found = await _first(mail_tasks[role], ([], []))
        chosen: dict[str, evidence.Mail] = {}
        for key in keys or [""]:
            message = (bidplan.governing(found, ref, scenario, sources[role].sender, domain, key)
                       or bidplan.governing(found, ref, scenario, sources[role].sender, domain))
            if message:
                chosen[message.page] = message
        record_type, task = CONTENT[role]
        items: list = []
        for message in sorted(chosen.values(), key=lambda m: parse.when(m.date, scenario.year), reverse=True):
            try:
                page = pages[parse.whole(message.page) - 1]
            except (parse.ParseError, IndexError):
                continue
            trace.event(role, "governing", sender=message.sender, date=message.date, reference=message.reference)
            filled = await evidence.read([page], task, record_type, trace=trace, name=role,
                                         context=f"Keys needed: {', '.join(keys)}" if keys else "")
            if filled:  # every record type here is one list of records
                items += getattr(filled, next(iter(record_type.model_fields)))
        if not chosen:
            notes.append(f"{role}: no governing message found")
        return items or None

    async def approval() -> None:
        if "discount_approval" not in mail_tasks:
            return
        _, found = await _first(mail_tasks["discount_approval"], ([], []))
        approving = [m for m in found if isinstance(m, evidence.ApprovalMail) and m.approves]
        message = bidplan.governing(approving, ref, scenario, sources["discount_approval"].sender, domain)
        if message:
            trace.event("discount_approval", "governing", sender=message.sender, date=message.date,
                        percent=message.percent, min_order_value=message.min_order_value)
        records.approval = bidplan.approval(message, notes)

    def used(kind: str) -> list[str]:
        return sorted({line.keys[kind] for line in tender_lines if line.keys.get(kind)})

    # ---- stage 2: the materials that fit, and the records the clarifications point to

    def wanted_text(line: bidplan.Line) -> str:
        derived = bidplan.needs_reserve(line)  # the stroke to match is not known before the end reserve is
        shown = [f"{key} {value}" for key, value in line.attributes.items()
                 if value and not (derived and key == "stroke")]
        return "- " + ", ".join(shown) + (" (stroke: any, it is still being derived)" if derived else "")

    async def candidates(group: str) -> list[evidence.Candidate]:
        wanted = "\n".join(wanted_text(line) for line in tender_lines if line.group == group)
        pages = await collect(erp, CANDIDATES_GOAL.format(group=repr(group), wanted=wanted), name=f"materials {group}",
                              deadline=stage_two, max_steps=40)
        found = await evidence.read(pages, "List every material shown, each once, with its five attributes and its "
                                    "status.", evidence.Candidates, trace=trace, name=f"materials {group}",
                                    thinking=False)
        return found.candidates if found else []

    groups = sorted({line.group for line in tender_lines if line.group})
    candidate_tasks = {group: start(candidates(group)) for group in groups}
    reserves_task = (start(content("technical_release", [revision]))
                     if any(bidplan.needs_reserve(line) for line in tender_lines) else None)
    keyed = {"rules": ("condition_rules", "condition_group"), "tariffs": ("packaging_tariffs", "packaging_tariff"),
             "commitments": ("delivery_commitments", "delivery_commitment"), "pools": ("setup_pools", "setup_pool"),
             "bonuses": ("project_bonus", "project_bonus")}
    record_tasks = {name: start(content(role, used(kind))) if used(kind) else None
                    for name, (role, kind) in keyed.items()}
    approval_task = start(approval())

    reserves = await _first(reserves_task)
    found_candidates = {group: await _first(task, []) for group, task in candidate_tasks.items()}
    chosen: dict[str, tuple[evidence.Candidate | None, str]] = {}

    def choose_all() -> None:
        for line in tender_lines:
            wanted = bidplan.requirement_attributes(line, revision, reserves, notes) if line.requirement else None
            chosen[line.position] = bidplan.choose(wanted, found_candidates.get(line.group, [])) if wanted \
                else (None, "unknown")

    choose_all()
    doubtful = sorted({line.group for line in tender_lines if chosen[line.position][1] == "none"})
    if doubtful and time.monotonic() < stage_two:  # no material fits: look a second time before declining to bid
        trace.event("research", "recheck", groups=doubtful)
        again = await asyncio.gather(*(candidates(group) for group in doubtful))
        for group, more in zip(doubtful, again):
            numbers = {c.material_number for c in more}
            found_candidates[group] = more + [c for c in found_candidates[group] if c.material_number not in numbers]
        choose_all()
    await _first(approval_task)
    trace.event("research", "stage_two", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1),
                chosen={p: (c.material_number if c else None, verdict) for p, (c, verdict) in chosen.items()})
    state["plan"] = bidplan.plan(ref, scenario, tender_lines, chosen, {}, records, list(notes))

    # ---- stage 3: the chosen materials' stock, lead times and prices, and the records those point to

    async def material_facts(number: str) -> evidence.MaterialFacts | None:
        pages = await collect(erp, MATERIAL_GOAL.format(number=number), name=f"material {number}",
                              deadline=stage_three, max_steps=45)
        return await evidence.read(pages, f"Report the facts of material {number}: stock, lead times, carton size, "
                                   "masses, metal price index and every price condition record with all its scales.",
                                   evidence.MaterialFacts, trace=trace, name=f"material {number}",
                                   context=f"Material wanted: {number}")

    numbers = sorted({c.material_number for c, _ in chosen.values() if c})
    fact_tasks = {number: start(material_facts(number)) for number in numbers}
    for name, task in record_tasks.items():
        setattr(records, name, await _first(task))
    facts = {number: found for number, task in fact_tasks.items() if (found := await _first(task))}
    state["plan"] = bidplan.plan(ref, scenario, tender_lines, chosen, facts, records, list(notes))

    fx_keys = sorted({c.fx_key.strip() or c.currency.strip() for f in facts.values() for c in f.conditions
                      if c.currency.strip() and "EUR" not in c.currency.upper()})
    index_codes = sorted({f.metal_index.strip() for f in facts.values() if f.metal_index.strip()})
    fx_task = start(content("fx_fixing", fx_keys)) if fx_keys else None
    index_task = start(content("metal_indices", index_codes)) if index_codes else None
    records.fx, records.indices = await _first(fx_task), await _first(index_task)
    state["plan"] = bidplan.plan(ref, scenario, tender_lines, chosen, facts, records, notes)
    trace.event("research", "done", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1),
                plan=state["plan"].model_dump(mode="json"))

content.content:
Atira Challenges CLI

Usage: atira <command> [options]   (or: node atira.mjs <command> [options])

Commands:
  login [--device] [--key <key>]
      Sign in through the browser (--device: with a code instead) and store a personal token, mode 0600; --key stores a team key where there is no GitHub sign-in
  logout
      Revoke the stored token on the server and forget it
  whoami
      Show who you are signed in as, your team and when the token expires
  token
      Print the token in use, for curl: curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)" ...
  upgrade
      Download the server's current CLI, check its SHA-256 and replace this file
  challenges
      List the challenges
  challenge <id>
      Print a challenge as Markdown: task, websites, rules, run contract, submitting, answer schema
  scout [--challenge <id>] [--env [--port <port>]]
      Print the published scouting logins for the public websites; --env prints shell exports (CHALLENGE_SCOUTING, CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS, each site's URL, and QWEN_BASE_U
  models proxy [--port <port>]
      Run a local proxy on 127.0.0.1 (port 8765) to the free models, QWEN_BASE_URL and CLEF_BASE_URL: it prints the exports
  test-run <dir> [--challenge <id>] [--dry-run] [--follow] [--no-open]
      Pack <dir>, run it once in the sandbox on the public data and open its run page; --follow prints its place in the queue, then streams its logs here
  submit <dir> [--challenge <id>] [--dry-run] [--follow] [--no-open]
      Pack <dir> and submit it for a ranked run, public and final: review, then one scored run on the public dataset; opens the team page, which follows both; --follow pr
  final [--best-of <1|3>] [--challenge <id>]
      Choose one final attempt or best of three before the final run starts; your own model keys cost up to 3×
  status [<id>] [--challenge <id>]
      Your latest submissions and test runs, or one submission (sub_), test run (reh_) or run (run_)
  logs <run> [--follow]
      Print a test or scored run's logs; --follow polls until the run has ended
  package <id> [--out <dir>]
      Show the package a test run (reh_ or run_), scored run or submission (sub_) of your team used, as uploaded: agent.json and each file's size; --out saves the .tar.gz
  cancel <run>
      Cancel a test or scored run that has not finished: its sandbox is removed and the run fails
  leaderboard [--challenge <id>]
      Print the leaderboard
  mcp
      Serve MCP on stdio, so a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ...) can list and debug your runs: why a run failed, logs by time, model calls, where the time we

Options:
  --challenge, -c <id>  The challenge (default: ATIRA_CHALLENGE, else the platform's first)
  --json                Machine-readable output on stdout, errors included

18	from playwright.async_api import BrowserContext, Dialog, Page
19	from pydantic_ai import RunContext
20	from tracing import Trace
21	
22	MAX_VIEW = 14000  # characters of a page shown at once; read_more pages through the rest
23	MAX_PAGES = 30  # pages keep_all_pages follows a paging control for
24	
25	# Closes modal <dialog>s and aria-modal popups through their own close button as soon as they open, and records
26	# what it closed. Links inside popups ("accept and continue") are never followed.
27	AUTO_CLOSE_JS = r"""
28	(() => {
29	  if (window.__arInit) return;
30	  window.__arInit = true;
31	  const CLOSE = /^(×|✕|✖|x|schließen|schliessen|close|dismiss|ausblenden|später|later|nicht jetzt|not now)$/i;
32	  const closed = (window.__arClosed = window.__arClosed || []);
33	  function closeButton(d) {
34	    for (const b of d.querySelectorAll('button,[role=button]')) {
35	      const name = (b.getAttribute('aria-label') || b.textContent || '').trim();
36	      if (CLOSE.test(name) || b.hasAttribute('data-close')) return b;
37	    }
38	    return null;
39	  }
40	  function check() {
41	    for (const d of document.querySelectorAll('dialog[open],[role=dialog][aria-modal=true],[role=alertdialog]')) {
42	      const modal = d.tagName !== 'DIALOG' || d.matches(':modal');
43	      if (!modal || d.dataset.arClosed) continue;
44	      const b = closeButton(d);
45	      if (!b) continue;
46	      d.dataset.arClosed = '1';
47	      closed.push((d.getAttribute('aria-label') || d.querySelector('h1,h2,h3')?.textContent || 'popup').trim());
48	      b.click();
49	      if (d.tagName === 'DIALOG' && d.open) d.close();
50	    }
51	  }
52	  const start = () => {
53	    check();
54	    new MutationObserver(check).observe(document.documentElement,
55	      {subtree: true, childList: true, attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open', 'aria-modal', 'style', 'class']});
56	  };
57	  if (document.documentElement) start(); else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', start);
58	})();
59	"""
60	
61	# "Slide to unlock" plus "I am not a robot" checks in any frame: drag the slider to its end, tick only boxes that
62	# are labelled as a robot check. Other checkboxes (terms, declarations) are left to the model.
63	HUMAN_CHECK_JS = r"""
64	() => {
65	  const ROBOT = /roboter|robot|mensch\b|human/i, SLIDE = /entsperr|unlock|zieh|slide|schieb/i;
66	  const labels = e => e.labels ? Array.from(e.labels).map(l => l.textContent) : [];
67	  const text = e => [e.getAttribute('aria-label') || '', ...labels(e)].join(' ');
68	  const done = [];
69	  for (const r of document.querySelectorAll('input[type=range]')) {
70	    const around = text(r) + ' ' + (r.parentElement ? r.parentElement.textContent : '');
71	    const max = r.max || '100';
72	    if (!SLIDE.test(around) || r.value === max || r.disabled) continue;
73	    r.value = max;
74	    r.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}));
75	    r.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
76	    done.push('unlock slider');
77	  }
78	  for (const c of document.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')) {
79	    if (c.checked || c.disabled || !ROBOT.test(text(c))) continue;
80	    c.click();
81	    done.push('robot check');
82	  }
83	  return done;
84	}
85	"""
86	
87	ERROR_PAGE = re.compile(r"vorübergehend nicht verfügbar|temporarily unavailable|service unavailable|bad gateway|"
88	                        r"gateway time-?out|internal server error|bitte versuchen sie es (später )?erneut",
89	                        re.IGNORECASE)
90	COOKIE = re.compile(r"cookie", re.IGNORECASE)
91	COOKIE_ANSWER = re.compile(r"akzeptier|accept|zustimm|agree|ablehn|reject|erlaub|allow|bestätig|confirm|ok\b",
92	                           re.IGNORECASE)
93	COOKIE_MINIMAL = re.compile(r"notwendig|erforderlich|necessary|essential|nur technisch|ablehnen|reject|decline",
94	                            re.IGNORECASE)
